resources.string: Requires a Tor daemon on this machine. Tor Browser (while running) or the tor service both listen on %1$s:%2$d.

Lookup queries enabled servers in order (after WKD); publish offers each publish-enabled server. keys.openpgp.org verifies emails but may reject v6/PQC keys; keys.pgpony.app accepts every key type PGPony makes.
Base URL (scheme + host, no trailing slash)
The server should speak the keys.openpgp.org VKS API; PGPony falls back to HKP (/pks/add) for publishing where VKS is missing.
Refresh keys from key servers automatically (every 12 hours while running)
The .pgpony format cross-restores with PGPony for iOS and Android; OpenKeychain backups restore too.
Everything that applies to PGPony on this computer.
Proxy, keyservers, and automatic key refresh.
Theme and language. Both take effect immediately.
Browses a standard `pass` store (a folder of .gpg files with .gpg-id recipient files) and decrypts entries with your keyring, software or hardware key. Read-only: PGPony never writes to the store.

No store here yet. PASSWORD_STORE_DIR is honored if you set it; otherwise add any folder on the Password Store tab.

5 to 600 seconds. The timer only clears the clipboard if it still holds what PGPony put there. If you copied something else, your clipboard is left alone. Note that a clipboard manager or a sync service (KDE Klipper, Windows cloud clipboard, macOS Universal Clipboard) may keep a copy PGPony cannot reach.
The whole window switches immediately, no restart. Text that comes from your keys or your files is shown as they store it and is never translated.

Key metadata lives in pgpony.db (the same Room schema as PGPony for Android); armored key material lives under keys/, one file per key half, mode 0600. Secret keys stay in their own passphrase (S2K) protection at rest. The store adds no crypto of its own.
Same OpenPGP engine and Room schema as PGPony for Android (vendored, not rewritten).
The desktop source is published with the 1.0 release. The Android app and the shared crypto cores are already public.
The rest of the family, by the same developer. Links open in your browser.
The same keyring everywhere: one OpenPGP engine and one backup format, from phone to desktop.
End-to-end encrypted messages and file transfer over OpenPGP. No account, no phone number.
File encryption and detached signing built on age. Encrypt to a GitHub username, sign with a security key.
Split a secret across backup cards. A threshold of them restores it; any single one reveals nothing.
Send files straight from one device to another over Wi-Fi. Encrypted end to end, with no server in between.
Self-destructing encrypted notes, sealed on your device and gone once they have been read.
Encrypted vaults on your phone, in the VeraCrypt container format, so the same vault opens on your computer.
A client for pass and passage password stores. Your passwords stay encrypted files in your own git repository.
Hash and verify files the way sha256sum does, with checksum files, folder checks and every common algorithm.
Tap an NFC tag and send its ID and contents to your own server. No account, no cloud.

Point PGPony at a `pass` store: a folder of OpenPGP-encrypted .gpg files, the layout the standard password-store tools use.

The store is read in place, so whatever syncs it (git, Syncthing, Nextcloud) keeps working. PGPony reads only: it never writes, moves, or re-encrypts anything in the folder. Entries are decrypted one at a time, when you open them. Browsing the tree reads filenames only.
Entry file is missing or unreadable.
No key in your keyring can open this entry. Import the secret key it\'s encrypted to, or pair the hardware key that holds it.
This entry is encrypted to a hardware key.
The paired card key for this entry isn\'t in your keyring.
PGPony can\'t generate codes from this URI. It isn\'t a TOTP URI, or its secret isn\'t valid base32. Use your authenticator app for this entry.
PGPony displays this setup URI but does not generate codes on this device. Copy it into an authenticator app.
This JVM has no HMAC-%1$s provider, so the code can\'t be generated here.
OpenPGP smart cards over USB: YubiKey 5, Token2, Nitrokey 3 and friends. Secrets live on the key and never touch this computer.
No PC/SC reader detected. Plug in the key (it enumerates as its own reader).
On Linux, install and start pcscd.
Insert the hardware key and choose Read card. PGPony reads the card\'s public slots only. Nothing is written to it.

Pairing records the card in your keyring so messages can be addressed to it and decrypt/sign route through the hardware. If the card\'s public key certificate is already in your keyring (import it or fetch from a key server), pairing links onto that row, offline-primary layouts included.
Generated on card and paired: %1$s. Export and BACK UP the public key; the secret keys cannot leave the card.
Remember the user PIN after a successful operation
Held in memory only, never written to disk. A wrong PIN, quitting the app, or Clear now drops it. The Admin PIN is never cached.
Wrong entries burn retry attempts. The card blocks after too many.
This ERASES every key on the card and resets both PINs to their defaults (123456 / 12345678). Keys generated on-card are unrecoverable. This cannot be undone.

Generates an Ed25519 signing key + Cv25519 encryption key ON the card. OVERWRITES the card\'s signature and decryption slots. The private keys never leave the hardware and CANNOT be backed up. Lose the card, lose the keys.
I understand this overwrites the card\'s keys and they can\'t be backed up

Off by default. When you turn it on, PGPony checks pgpony.app once a day for a newer version. Nothing about you or your keys is sent, and your proxy setting is followed.
You are running the latest version.

Off by default. When you turn it on, PGPony serves your authentication keys to ssh over a local socket, like ssh-agent but backed by your keyring. It never holds keys between requests, and a protected key is asked for each time. macOS and Linux only in this release.
The SSH agent is not available on Windows in this release. The platform's ssh expects a named pipe the app cannot serve yet.
ssh asked PGPony to sign with %1$s, which is passphrase-protected.

Off by default. When on, PGPony watches the folders you name and encrypts each new file to the recipients you pick. It is encrypt-only and uses public keys only, so a rule that runs while you are away never needs a passphrase or a card, and can at worst encrypt. macOS, Linux and Windows.
No rules yet. Add one to watch a folder.
No usable recipients. Import a public key first.
The original is removed with no undo. Leave off unless you are sure.
Another program is using the reader. Close it (such as GnuPG or OpenSC) and rescan.
The reader service reported a problem.
Move a key onto the card

This writes an existing key onto the card and overwrites the card's key slots. Unlike a key generated on the card, this one already existed off the card, so keep your backup safe. The card's PINs are unchanged.
No RSA keypair with a private key is in your keyring. Generate or import one first.

ML-DSA signing reads the whole file into memory and is limited to 512 MB. Sign a smaller file, or pick a classical signing key.
This needs the private key, and only the public key is in your keyring.
This key lives on a hardware key, so it can’t be edited from here.

Ask you to type %1$s before a key is deleted, a subkey or User ID is removed, or all data is cleared. On by default.
Only Ed25519 and X25519 subkeys can be added to a v6 key.
A v4 key takes the ML-KEM-768 post-quantum subkey only. ML-KEM-1024 needs a v6 key.
A post-quantum signing subkey needs a v6 key.
No passphrase. On this computer the key file is protected only by its file permissions, so anyone who can use your account can use the key.
Revoking publishes a signature that tells your correspondents to stop using this subkey once they refresh your key. It can’t be undone.
I understand every key is destroyed now, with no recovery window.
PGPony will close now. The next launch starts fresh.

Also removed: every PGPony setting (key servers, network, SSH agent, watch folders, password store), the watch rules and the cached card PIN. Your password store folder and files you saved elsewhere are not touched.
Signs as %1$s, this key’s signing default. Enter that key’s passphrase.

Each key serves its newest authentication subkey that cannot also sign or certify: Ed25519, RSA, or ECDSA on NIST P-256, P-384 or P-521, a classical subkey on a post-quantum key included. Add one in Key Detail or when generating a key. RSA keys still answer the older SHA-1 ssh-rsa request from servers that ask for it.

The Comment line in ASCII-armored output. It applies to the app, the pgpony command, the git signing shim and watch folders.

How long PGPony keeps a key passphrase or the card PIN in memory after you enter it. One setting covers the app, the SSH agent and git signing through pgpony-gpg. Nothing is written to disk, and quitting PGPony forgets everything.

Move keys or a full backup between two computers on the same network. One computer waits, the other connects, and you compare a code on both screens. Nothing is kept after you close this window.

Off by default. When on, pgpony-gpg asks this window to sign git commits, tags and push certificates with a passphrase-protected key. PGPony signs nothing else this way, asks for the passphrase unless you entered it to sign earlier in this session, and shows a notification for every signature. When on, PGPony sends the fingerprint of every key in your keyring to each key server enabled for lookup, about once a day, through your proxy if you set one. Off for new installs.
